title: Activation stakeholder slate and timebox guidelines (working)
content:
Purpose

Quick, messy working doc capturing a compact pattern for scheduling, stewarding, and timeboxing small-batch activations (micro-exposures, canaries, and A/B cohorts) that involve 3+ functions. This is intentionally lightweight: the goal is a repeatable agenda and a default set of communication artifacts so teams stop inventing unique rituals for every minor rollout.

Scope
- Applies to features that touch the inference runtime, model routing, or output shaping that carry behavioral risk (LLM hallucination/regression, latency cliff, cost spike) or cross-team dependencies (billing, SRE, Legal).
- Not intended for major platform launches or infra migrations that require the full release conductor runbook.

High-level pattern (one-paragraph)
Create a 3-phase, timeboxed activation slate: dry-rehearsal (0.5–1 day), micro-exposure (4–24 hours), evaluate-and-commit (1–3 days). For each phase assign a single Steward (the "steward baton") plus a backup. The Steward coordinates comms, decides on pause/scale-up, and logs decisions in the activation ledger (linked Confluence/JIRA). Use a simple watchlist of 6 telemetry signals (latency P95, error-rate, semantic-regression, token-cost, traffic-entropy, customer-affected-rate). If any signal trips a pre-agreed threshold, the Steward triggers an immediate pause and the emergency review call.

Stakeholder slate (roles & responsibilities)
- Steward (primary): product-console PM for the feature. Coordinates; has final go/no-go between timeboxes.
- Steward (backup): engineering lead (serving/runtime).
- Observability owner: SRE/observability engineer — owns dashboards and alert tuning for the run.
- Model owner: Applied ML engineer — owns quality checks, evaluation prompts, ground truth sets.
- Cost owner: FinOps / infra cost-ops — watches token/cycle cost signals.
- Customer comms: Customer Success lead — drafts comms if impacted customers are detected.
- Legal/compliance contact (if PII/privacy risk): Legal reviewer on-call.

Default timebox template (short notation)
- Dry-rehearsal: 0.5–1 day — internal smoke tests, synthetic traffic, runbook rehearsal, chatops slash commands verified.
- Micro-exposure: 4–24 hours — 0.5%–5% traffic depending on risk. Live telemetry, human-in-loop sampling if available.
- Evaluate-and-commit: 1–3 days — deep analysis of signals, spot manual review, decision to promote/roll back or scale cohort.

Concrete operational checklist (what to do during each timebox)
Dry-rehearsal:
- Verify routing config applied to test cohort (routing-id).
- Run synthetic suite: latency, throughput, model-quality fuzz tests.
- Confirm all alert thresholds deployed and visible in the steward dashboard.
- Execute the Slack rehearsal message template (see below) to confirm stakeholders can respond inside the SLA.
- Confirm canary traffic throttle controls are set and testable (kill-switch verified).

Micro-exposure (live):
- Start at minimal slice size (0.5%); capture 100–200 representative requests for manual review in first hour.
- Observability owner watches latency P95, request failures, and queue depth for first 30m with 5m cadence updates.
- Model owner runs spot-eval: 50 seeded prompts from golden set every 2 hours.
- Cost owner monitors per-token unit cost and projected 24h burn rate; flag if >1.5x baseline.
- Steward posts hourly status updates for first 6 hours, then 4h cadence thereafter.

Evaluate-and-commit:
- Synthesize: telemetry summary, sample failure cases, manual-eval pass-rate, cost delta.
- Decision matrix: promote, extend micro-exposure, pivot (config change), or rollback.
- If promoting, pick incremental exposure steps (2x, 5x) with timeboxes and updated watch thresholds.

Watchlist signals & suggested thresholds (starter values)
- Latency P95: > +30% vs baseline --> warn; > +100% --> pause.
- Error rate (5xx + model exceptions): > 0.5% absolute increase --> warn; >1.5% --> pause.
- Semantic regression (manual-eval fail rate): >5% absolute drop in pass-rate of golden prompts --> pause and investigate.
- Token-cost per request: projected >1.5x --> consult cost owner (possible throttle).
- Traffic-entropy / input-shift: sudden spike in atypical requests (>3x baseline) --> surface to model owner.
- Customer-affected-rate: measurable number of distinct customers with degraded outputs (>=3) --> customer comms.

Escalation & immediate-actions ladder
1) Steward-level pause and 5m triage with on-call SRE and model owner.
2) If unresolved in 30m, convene emergency review (15m) with PM, Eng lead, SRE, CS.
3) If unresolved in 90m, escalate to Director-level (product + engineering) and trigger rollback to safe baseline.

Templates (copy/paste)
Slack start message (Dry-rehearsal)
"[STEWARD] DRY-REHEARSAL START: feature=<<feature-name>> | routing=<<routing-id>> | duration=4h | oncall=#observability | ack please (steward-baton)."

Slack launch message (Micro-exposure)
"[STEWARD] MICRE-EXPOSURE START: feature=<<feature-name>> | cohort=0.5% | watchlist active: p95/err/semantic/cost | kill-switch=<<link>> | hourly updates first 6h. Ping @sre-oncall @model-owner @finops if anomalies."

Quick decision record format (one line to append to activation ledger)
"2026-02-19 10:15Z | micro-exposure start | steward=Priya Nair | cohort=0.5% | note=initial smoke OK; p95 +10%"

Steward rotation (example cadence)
- Week 0: Product PM (Priya) steward -> dry-rehearsal + micro-exposure start
- Week 1: Engineering lead (Marcus) steward -> evaluate-and-commit
- Rationale: rotation reduces single-person chokepoints; steward baton passed with a 10-minute sync.

Rehearsal script (5-step)
1. Verify dashboards: all graphs update with test traffic within 2 minutes.
2. Trigger synthetic error (low-severity) and confirm alert fires, paging flow tested.
3. Run token-cost spike sim: verify cost owner sees projected burn and confirms alert.
4. Practice rollback: execute kill-switch and validate traffic reverts in <3 minutes.
5. Post-rehearsal retro: capture 3 actions (what failed, who was slow, what to automate).

Notes-to-self / open questions
- How much of this can be automated in the console UI (default templates + one-click rehearsal)? Good product slot.
- Do we need a short-form legal clearance checklist for PII-sensitive prompts — maybe a 3-question gating card?
- Consider adding an "interpretability" quick-sample step for rerankers where human-marked relevance is required.

Action items (current)
- Alex: build a default watchlist dashboard for the steward view (JIRA-1301).
- Marcus: add kill-switch endpoint and test harness (GH PR linked).
- Leah: draft the short-form customer comms templates for CS (first draft due 2026-02-28).
- Priya: pilot this pattern on feature PR-513 starting next week.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts used in pilot
- Golden prompt set (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/golden-prompts
- Pilot routing config: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-configs/pull/89
- Activation ledger template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/activation-ledger-template

End of working notes.

(very much a scratchpad — please add edits inline; call out anything that feels like a heavy lift so we can scope automation work.)
